topic: Change of Basis: Viewing the World through Different Lenses

sections.title: The Perspective Problem: Maya and the Drone
lecture_lines: Maya and her drone see the world differently.
The drone is tilted, viewing targets from its perspective.
We need a translator between these two viewpoints.
animations: Show Maya at the origin on a standard grid (Sky Blue: #87CEEB). Label "Maya's View" (#FFFFFF).
Overlay a Drone-aligned grid (Gold: #FFD700) rotated 45 degrees. Label "Drone's View" (#FFFFFF).
Plot a red vector (#FF0000) pointing 1 unit along the Drone's forward axis. Display coordinates: Drone: [1, 0] and Maya: [0.7, 0.7].

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
lecture_lines: A basis provides building blocks for any point.
Usually, we use the standard blue grid.
But any set of independent vectors works.
animations: Show standard basis vectors i and j (Blue: #87CEEB) on a grid.
Overlay two new basis vectors b1 and b2 (Gold: #FFD700) pointing in different directions.
Show a target point P (#FFFFFF) and highlight how it's a sum of either basis set.

sections.title: The Core Concept: One Vector, Two Names
lecture_lines: This red vector exists independently in space.
In the standard grid, its coordinates are three, two.
Now, we switch to a different basis grid.
Relative to this new grid, its coordinates change.
The vector stays fixed; only the coordinates change.
animations: Show a single red vector (#FF0000) alone in empty space to represent physical reality.
Fade in [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/the.svg] standard blue grid (#87CEEB) and label the vector coordinates [3, 2].
Morph [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/the.svg] grid into a gold slanted basis (#FFD700) and update the label to [1, 1].

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (The Translator)
lecture_lines: Express the new basis vectors in standard coordinates.
Arrange these vectors as columns in matrix P.
Multiplying by P converts coordinates back to standard.
animations: Display a large matrix symbol P labeled "The Translator" (Green: #00FF00) along with the translator icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/translator.svg].
Expand P to show its columns as the new basis vectors in gold (#FFD700).
Show the matrix-vector product P * [x]_New (Gold: #FFD700).
Display the equals sign followed by the standard coordinate vector [x]_Std (Sky Blue: #87CEEB).
Highlight the complete formula P * [x]_New = [x]_Std with a white flash (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: The Visual Transformation: Warping the Grid
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication physically warps the entire grid.
The standard grid morphs into the new basis.
Watch how the coordinate lines bend and stretch.
The vector arrow stays still while the grid shifts.
Coordinates change inversely to keep the vector fixed.
animations: Show a standard square grid [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] (Sky Blue: #87CEEB).
Morph the standard grid into a sheared/rotated grid (Gold: #FFD700) via matrix multiplication.
Emphasize the bending and stretching of the grid lines during the transformation.
Keep the red target vector (#FF0000) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/arrow.svg] fixed in space while the grid shifts.
Display updating coordinate values (x,y) to (a,b) as the grid deforms.

sections.title: Practical Application: Why Bother?
lecture_lines: Some problems are simpler in a custom basis.
An eagle's flight is easy along its path.
Aligning the basis simplifies complex diagonal motion.
animations: Show an Eagle (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eagle.svg] flying diagonally on a standard grid with a complex velocity vector.
Rotate the entire grid until one axis aligns with the Eagle's [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eagle.svg] flight path.
Show the new velocity vector as a simple one-component value (Speed, 0).

sections.title: Summary & The 'Golden Rule' Formula
lecture_lines: Use P to move from new to standard.
The inverse, P-inverse, takes us back again.
This formula links every perspective together.
Coordinates are relative, but the vector is absolute.
Choose the basis that makes your math easy.
animations: Display the main formula: [x]_Std = P * [x]_New in bright Green (#00FF00).
Display the reverse formula: [x]_New = P^-1 * [x]_Std in Orange (#FF8C00).
Show a flowchart: [Drone View] -> [Matrix P] -> [Maya View] (#FFFFFF).
Show the inverse path: [Maya View] -> [P^-1] -> [Drone View] (#FFFFFF).
Final summary: Fade out grids, leaving the formulas and the "Translator" concept.
